$comment: Allow-list for the axe passes in e2e/a11y.spec.ts.
Every entry is a DEFERRAL, not an absolution: it names one axe rule, the
pass and routes it applies to, and a node-level predicate that must match.
A violation is only suppressed when EVERY one of its nodes is matched by
some exception — a single unmatched node fails the test and prints the
node. That is what makes this a ratchet: the known failures stay quiet,
but any NEW node (a different colour pair, a different element) is red.
An exception without a predicate (no `contrast`, no `htmlIncludes`) is
rejected at load time, so nobody can accidentally mute a whole rule.
Fields:
id            — stable handle, named when the entry goes stale
pass          — 'preview' (the [data-docs-preview] region),
'code' (the CodeExample CodePanel: toolbar + Shiki) or
'playground' (the PlaygroundConfigurator specimen)
rule          — axe rule id
routes        — the full routes it applies to, e.g.
'/blocks/components/calendar'. Each must be a route the
spec scans; there is no wildcard
contrast      — for color-contrast: the exact fg/bg pair axe computed
htmlIncludes  — every string must appear in axe's `node.html`: the
outerHTML, but only the opening tag once the element is
long (and a long tag's attribute values are cut too), so
a container's children are usually not in it
summary       — optional: the node's exact failure summary, whitespace
collapsed. htmlIncludes pins which node fails; this pins
how, so a second reason to fail is not covered
reason        — why this is not fixed here
ref           — where the decision / follow-up lives
An entry that matches nothing on a route it names fails that route's test:
when a row gets fixed, delete its entry (or drop the route that no longer
needs it).

exceptions.summary: Fix any of the following: Element has children which are not allowed: button[aria-label], button
exceptions.reason: Library structure: CalendarWeekGrid puts its weekday-head and event buttons directly under role="grid", outside any row or gridcell (30 owned buttons on this page). Follow-up A restructures the week view.

exceptions.summary: Fix any of the following: Element has children which are not allowed: button[aria-label]
exceptions.reason: Library structure: CalendarYearGrid's 12 month buttons sit directly under role="grid", which has no rows at all. Follow-up A restructures the year view.

exceptions.summary: Fix any of the following: Required ARIA children role not present: cell, columnheader, gridcell, rowheader
exceptions.reason: CustomDayCell demo: CalendarDay renders the dayCell snippet's output directly inside role="row", so these 6 rows hold no gridcell, and the dayCell contract does not say who owns the cell. Follow-up A states that contract. LIMIT: axe reports a row by its opening tag only, and that tag is the same for every month row without week numbers in a variant that adds no row class (default and ghost), so this entry would also hide such a row elsewhere on this page that lost all its cells.

exceptions.summary: Fix any of the following: Element has children which are not allowed: button[aria-label]
exceptions.reason: Library structure: with onEventClick, CalendarMultiDayBar renders buttons in a container outside the week rows, so the month grid owns them directly (2 on the playground). Follow-up A moves them into the grid's row/cell structure.

Outside-month day numbers use text-quaternary, 1.96:1. These days are enabled buttons that select on click, so WCAG 1.4.3's exemption for inactive components does not apply. Follow-up C moves them to a darker ink that reaches AA in both modes and stays subdued.
The same outside-month day numbers on the playground's tinted stage, 1.90:1; enabled buttons, not inactive. Follow-up C.
Week numbers (role="rowheader") use text-quaternary, 1.96:1. They are static information, not an inactive component. Follow-up C.
Event labels on a #8b5cf6 category: getContrastTextColor picks white (4.23:1) by a brightness threshold, where black reaches 4.96:1. Follow-up B makes it pick the higher WCAG ratio.
Event labels on a #3b82f6 category: getContrastTextColor picks white (3.68:1) where black reaches 5.71:1. Follow-up B.
CustomDayCell heatmap demo dims outside-month cells with opacity-20, 1.13:1. They are plain divs, not a UI component, so no inactive exemption applies. Follow-up D restyles the demo.
CustomDayCell heatmap demo, level-1 cells: emerald-700 on emerald-500/15, 4.47:1. Follow-up D restyles the demo.
CustomDayCell heatmap demo, level-4 cell: white on emerald-500/75, 2.03:1. Follow-up D restyles the demo.
